content: I need help with a workstation that keeps shutting down during rendering jobs. I also need to understand repair eligibility and replacement timelines.

To assist you effectively, could you please provide the following details:
1. The make and model of the workstation.
2. The operating system and any error messages you receive when it shuts down.
3. How long the workstation has been experiencing this issue.
4. Any recent hardware or software changes made before the issue started.
5. Whether the workstation is under warranty or any extended service plan.

Regarding repair eligibility and replacement timelines:
- If the workstation is still under the manufacturer’s warranty or a service contract, repairs are usually covered unless the issue is due to accidental damage or unauthorized modifications.
- Out-of-warranty repairs may incur costs, and depending on the age and severity of the problem, replacement might be more cost-effective.
- Typical repair turnaround times vary from a few days to a couple of weeks, depending on parts availability and service center workload.
- Replacement timelines depend on procurement and setup processes but can range from one week to several weeks.

Once I have more information about your specific workstation and issue, I can help diagnose the problem and advise on repair and replacement options.

Intermittent shutdowns during rendering usually point to thermal stress, power delivery instability, or GPU failure. Since a temporary GPU was already tested, we should compare shutdown frequency before and after the swap. I also need to know whether the system powers off completely or shows blue screen errors.
The system powers off instantly without a blue screen. After the temporary GPU was installed, crashes became less frequent but still happen during long render queues.
Likely causes: power supply issues or overheating; consider testing PSU and monitoring CPU/GPU temperatures during renders.

That suggests either the original GPU contributed to the issue or the power supply is unstable under sustained load. I recommend running a PSU stress test and checking motherboard event logs. If diagnostics confirm hardware failure, we can initiate an RMA with either on-site service or depot repair depending on warranty coverage.
What is the office location?
I don't know
The registered office location is Lahore, Pakistan. That region supports on-site diagnostics for enterprise systems if the warranty is active.
We ran a PSU stress test and voltage dipped below tolerance during GPU rendering. Does that qualify for direct replacement instead of component repair?
Yes, PSU failure under load typically qualifies for direct replacement if warranty or service contract covers hardware faults.

A failed PSU can qualify for advanced replacement if the warranty tier includes expedited hardware exchange. Since your downtime requirement is strict, advanced replacement is preferable to mail-in repair. The support team may still request diagnostic logs and photos of the PSU label before approving the RMA.
If replacement stock is unavailable locally, can the unit be shipped to another repair center?
Yes, replacement units can be shipped to another repair center if local stock is unavailable.
Why can't the customer ship hardware internationally?
I don't know

Your procurement policy prevents international hardware shipping, so the repair must stay within supported domestic service channels. In that case, on-site PSU replacement is the safest option if local inventory exists.
The vendor requested motherboard logs and thermal reports. I can provide both today. They also asked whether the BIOS was recently modified.
The BIOS was not recently modified. Logs and thermal reports will be provided today as requested.

Providing the motherboard logs and thermal reports should speed up approval. Since the BIOS was updated recently, include the update version and installation date because firmware changes can affect warranty troubleshooting procedures.
The support portal now shows pending approval for an on-site technician. They estimate three business days for dispatch.
Pending approval is for on-site technician dispatch, estimated to occur within three business days.
When was the FalconPro Z8 purchased?
I don't know
The FalconPro Z8 was purchased on March 12, 2025. That purchase date should still place it within most enterprise hardware warranty periods.
The vendor approved an on-site PSU replacement but denied full chassis replacement. They believe the motherboard is stable.
The vendor approved on-site PSU replacement but denied chassis replacement, believing the motherboard is stable.

That outcome is consistent with the stress-test evidence. If the shutdowns stop after PSU replacement, the case can close without depot repair. Keep the temporary GPU installed during validation testing to isolate variables.
The technician visit is scheduled for Monday morning. They requested the current system configuration and active GPU details.
Current system configuration includes temporary GPU installed; exact system specs not provided in the conversation.
What temporary hardware change was installed last week?
Temporary GPU was installed last week to reduce shutdown frequency during rendering.
You should document that a temporary replacement GPU was installed last week for testing purposes. That helps the technician understand why crash frequency changed during diagnostics.
If the PSU replacement fails to resolve the issue, would the next escalation step be depot repair or motherboard replacement on-site?
Next escalation would likely be depot repair since motherboard replacement on-site was denied by the vendor.

The next step would likely be motherboard replacement on-site if logs continue showing power instability. Depot repair is usually reserved for repeated failures involving multiple subsystems or unavailable field parts.
Understood. I will keep the render queue active after the repair so we can monitor stability under full load.
Understood. Keep the render queue active post-repair to monitor system stability under full load.
